digest.component_or_area: snapshot store cache layer (tickets tree materialization)
propositions: Every attested gate resolution materializes a fresh full copy (~620 MiB, 69,984 blobs) of the tickets tree with no hardlinking or delta against prior entries, because the cache key (tickets-branch tip) advances every ~26 seconds with zero reuse.
A one-file delta in a 300-file tree produces five separate inode copies across five sequential resolutions, yielding ~300x write amplification per resolution on the actual 69,984-blob tree.

The snapshot store cache design (ADR 0005 D2) assumes immutable SHAs as cache keys are perfect and have reuse; the tickets key violates this assumption, behaving as an append-only log rather than a bounded reclaimable cache.

Hardlinking unchanged paths between adjacent tickets SHAs and materializing only changed paths via delta_tree reduces write amplification and reclaims cache properties while preserving content integrity via attestation oracles.

Byte accounting must distinguish entry_size (reporting), exclusive_size (inode-deduplicated increment for populate/evict), and distinct_bytes (ground truth sweep), because st_size/nlink as an increment credits bytes still on disk, making eviction watermarks stop short of their target.
